skill.description: Purchase proxy access with USDC on Base, manage access tokens, and verify regional egress through TLS HTTP CONNECT.
skill.summary: Quote approved proxy purchases, protect access tokens, and test regional egress with x402socks.
skill.author: x402socks

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are Markdown, local signing, private token storage, or disclosed HTTPS service requests. Confirmed transport risks expose credentials when plaintext proxy modes or insecure API overrides are enabled; newline handling also permits curl configuration injection. No evidence found of malicious exfiltration intent or prompt injection.

remediation.issue: Legacy proxy modes and insecure API overrides transmit reusable credentials without encryption.
remediation.suggestion: Remove plaintext credential transports, or restrict them to authenticated encrypted tunnels and loopback test endpoints. Keep certificate-verified TLS CONNECT as the default.

remediation.issue: Environment tokens and endpoint URLs can inject new curl configuration lines.
remediation.suggestion: Reject CR, LF, and control characters before building curl configuration. Validate token syntax and parse endpoint URLs before reading credentials.

content.user_title: Manage Paid Proxy Access With x402socks
content.value_statement: Agents may need regional egress without managing a long-term proxy subscription. This skill guides approved USDC purchases, token management, and TLS proxy verification.
actual_capabilities: Fetch service health, live exit availability, package prices, and entitlements through the shell helper.
Decode live x402 challenges and check quoted amounts against an optional approved USDC cap.
Provide TypeScript payment examples that restrict signing to approved network, asset, recipient, domain, and amount.
Save, validate, inspect, rotate, and recover proxy tokens using private local storage.
Test egress through a selected healthy exit with certificate-verified TLS CONNECT by default.
Provide TLS proxy integration examples for curl, Python, Node.js, Playwright, and Chrome.
limitations: Purchasing requires a funded Base wallet, signing access, and a separate x402 client; the shell helper does not execute purchases.
Live prices, exit availability, session limits, and data caps depend on the external service.
SOCKS5, plaintext CONNECT, and insecure API overrides can expose credentials; TLS does not guarantee anonymity from the proxy operator.
The helper requires curl and Python; payment and browser integrations require additional libraries or tools.

use_cases.title: Check Regional Browser Behavior
use_cases.description: Configure a TLS proxy for Playwright tests and verify that requests leave through the selected region.

use_cases.title: Plan an Approved Data Collection Job
use_cases.description: Compare current proxy packages for permitted collection work and request approval before authorizing payment.

use_cases.title: Restore Existing Proxy Access
use_cases.description: Diagnose token validity, rotate exposed credentials, or recover a lost token using proof from the paying wallet.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Available Proxy Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Check x402socks health, available TLS exits, and current packages. Summarize options without accessing wallet secrets or making a purchase.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect the service before spending.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Purchase Approval
prompt_templates.prompt: Quote [package_id] with a maximum of [amount] USDC. Record all payment terms and entitlements, then wait for explicit approval before signing.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a TLS Proxy Exit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my existing token file to validate access and test [exit_id] through TLS CONNECT. Report the egress comparison without displaying credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Guarded Proxy Purchasing
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the TypeScript payment example for [application]. Pin approved terms before signing, require purchase approval, save tokens privately, and redact secrets from diagnostics.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: integrate payment approval and credential handling.

output_examples.input: Prepare an approval for a package without purchasing it.
output: Approval draft: package, live price, duration, data allowance, and session limit recorded.
Payment terms: scheme, network, asset, recipient, signing domain, and maximum amount recorded.
State: waiting for explicit approval; no authorization signed and no payment submitted.

output_examples.input: Explain the next steps after payment settled but provisioning failed.
output: Keep the settlement transaction hash and confirm access to the paying wallet.
Prepare the recovery message, sign it, and pass the signature privately to the recovery helper.
Save the replacement token without displaying it, then validate access before testing an exit.

best_practices: Approve the full live payment terms and a spending cap before signing; stop when the challenge differs.
Use certificate-verified TLS CONNECT and private token files; reject control characters in environment credentials and endpoint overrides.
Keep settlement proof and validate existing access before retrying; use recovery instead of paying twice.
anti_patterns: Automatically pay from cached package prices or accept changed recipients, assets, networks, or signing domains.
Paste wallet keys or live proxy tokens into chat, command arguments, source control, or logs.
Disable certificate verification or treat SOCKS5 and plaintext CONNECT as encrypted alternatives.

faq.question: What is required to purchase access?
faq.answer: You need USDC on Base, an accessible wallet signer, and an x402 client. The helper handles discovery and token management, not payment execution.

faq.question: Does the skill require approval before spending?
faq.answer: Yes. Its instructions require explicit approval and comparison of the live challenge against approved terms before signing.

faq.question: Which proxy transport should I use?
faq.answer: Prefer certificate-verified TLS CONNECT on port 3129. SOCKS5 and plaintext CONNECT expose the reusable token on the client-to-proxy connection.

faq.question: Which tools and clients are documented?
faq.answer: The helper uses Bash, curl, and Python. References cover Foundry cast, TypeScript and Python payments, Node.js, Playwright, and Chrome.

faq.question: Does a different egress IP guarantee anonymity?
faq.answer: No. An egress check verifies routing, not anonymity. The proxy operator and destination may still observe identifying information.

faq.question: What should I do after losing a token?
faq.answer: Use the settlement transaction hash and paying wallet to sign a recovery message. Save the replacement privately rather than purchasing again.
